chunks: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuha, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The bare one who has no garment, if he finds a pit, enters it and prostrates in it and bows."

key_terms.الْعَارِي: The bare one (one who has no clothing)
key_terms.حُفْرَة: Pit or hole in the ground

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying if one has no clothes to wear?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-istihlal* (validity through necessity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the lack of clothing is excused by utilizing the earth itself as a covering. It highlights the practical flexibility of prayer conditions, allowing the worshipper to perform ruku' and sujood within a pit to maintain modesty (*awrah*) when no garment is available. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in acts of worship.
